content: 1. Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, has the potential to increase the effects or levels of OCT2 substrates. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Vemurafenib decreases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 3. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the level or effect of venetoclax by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 4. Verapamil increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Viloxazine, a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor, increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates as clinically indicated. 6. Vinblastine increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Vincristine increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Vinorelbine increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Voriconazole increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Zafirlukast increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the level or effect of zanubrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib to 80 mg PO BID when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. Resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 12. Zileuton increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ziprasidone increases the level or effect of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Immune System Disorders: 14. Anaphylactic reactions and hypersensitivity have been reported. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers is contraindicated. 15. Familial short QT syndrome is a contraindication, as isavuconazole shortens the QTc interval in a concentration-dependent manner. 16. Infusion-related reactions, including hypotension, dyspnea, chills, dizziness, paresthesia, and hypoesthesia, have been reported. Discontinue the infusion if these reactions occur. 17. Isavuconazonium sulfate may cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant women. Anaphylactic reactions, including fatal outcomes, have been reported during treatment. Symptoms such as dyspnea, hypotension, generalized erythema with flushing, and urticaria often occur shortly after treatment initiation. 18. Based on animal studies, fetal harm may occur when administered to pregnant women. No human data are available to evaluate the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. 19. Isavuconazole was detected in the milk of lactating rats following IV administration, suggesting the drug may be present in human milk. Breastfeeding should be discontinued during treatment. Administration and Storage: 20. Switching between IV and oral formulations is acceptable, as bioequivalence has been demonstrated. A loading dose is not required when switching between formulations. 21. Oral capsules should be swallowed whole and not chewed, crushed, dissolved, or opened. They can be taken with or without food. 22. Capsules should be stored at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with excursions permitted between 15–30°C (59–86°F). Keep capsules in their original packaging to protect them from moisture. General Information: 23. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only.
